Pandas — Write the Code Questions
Topic 1: Series and DataFrame Basics | Topic 2: Reading and Writing Files

TOPIC 1 — Series and DataFrame Basics

Q1. Create a Series from a list

Ravi, Priya, Arjun, Meena, and Kiran scored the following marks in Python exam: 72, 88, 65, 91, 79.

Write code to:

a) Create a Series called python_marks with student names as the index and marks as values.

b) Print the Series.

c) Print only Arjun's mark by using his name as the label.

d) Print only the marks of Priya and Meena together in one statement.

Expected output:

Ravi     72
Priya    88
Arjun    65
Meena    91
Kiran    79
dtype: int64

65

Priya    88
Meena    91
dtype: int64


---

Q2. Series from a dictionary and basic operations

A dictionary stores the number of assignments submitted by each student:

{'Ravi': 8, 'Priya': 10, 'Arjun': 6, 'Meena': 10, 'Kiran': 7}


Write code to:

a) Create a Series submissions from this dictionary.

b) Print the student who submitted the most assignments using idxmax().

c) Print how many students submitted fewer than 8 assignments.

d) Add 1 bonus submission to everyone and print the updated Series.

Expected output:

Priya

2

Ravi      9
Priya    11
Arjun     7
Meena    11
Kiran     8
dtype: int64


---

Q3. Series attributes

Given the Series:
python
attendance = pd.Series([85.5, 92.0, 78.3, 95.1, 88.6],
                       index=['Ravi', 'Priya', 'Arjun', 'Meena', 'Kiran'])


Write code to print each of the following on a separate line:

a) The data type of the Series.

b) The shape of the Series.

c) The total number of elements.

d) All the index labels.

e) All the values as a NumPy array.

Expected output:

float64
(5,)
5
Index(['Ravi', 'Priya', 'Arjun', 'Meena', 'Kiran'], dtype='object')
[85.5 92.  78.3 95.1 88.6]


---

Q4. Series statistical methods

The internal assessment marks of 5 students are: 34, 28, 40, 22, 36.
Index is: Ravi, Priya, Arjun, Meena, Kiran.

Write code to:

a) Create the Series ia_marks.
b) Print the mean, median, minimum, maximum, and standard deviation (rounded to 2 decimal places).
c) Print the full statistical summary using a single method.

Expected output:

Mean   : 32.0
Median : 34.0
Min    : 22
Max    : 40
Std    : 6.93

count     5.000000
mean     32.000000
std       6.928203
min      22.000000
25%      28.000000
50%      34.000000
75%      36.000000
max      40.000000
dtype: float64

Write code to create a DataFrame df with the following data and print it:


Name     RollNo   Maths   Physics   City
Ravi       101      85       76     Hyderabad
Priya      102      92       88     Chennai
Arjun      103      78       82     Bangalore
Meena      104      95       90     Hyderabad
Kiran      105      88       79     Pune


After creating the DataFrame:

a) Print only the first 3 rows.

b) Print the shape, column names, and data types.

Expected output:

    Name  RollNo  Maths  Physics       City
0   Ravi     101     85       76  Hyderabad
1  Priya     102     92       88    Chennai
2  Arjun     103     78       82  Bangalore
3  Meena     104     95       90  Hyderabad
4  Kiran     105     88       79       Pune

    Name  RollNo  Maths  Physics       City

2  Arjun     103     78       82  Bangalore

Q6. Add, compute, and drop columns

Using the same student DataFrame from Q5:

a) Add a new column Total which is the sum of Maths and Physics.

b) Add a new column Average which is Total divided by 2.

c) Add a new column Grade where Average >= 90 gets 'O', Average >= 80 gets 'A', and the rest get 'B'. Use pd.cut or np.select.

d) Drop the Total column.

e) Print the final DataFrame.

Expected output:

    Name  RollNo  Maths  Physics  Average Grade
0   Ravi     101     85       76     80.5     A
1  Priya     102     92       88     90.0     O
2  Arjun     103     78       82     80.0     A
3  Meena     104     95       90     92.5     O
4  Kiran     105     88       79     83.5     A


---

d) Print the last 2 rows using tail().

e) Print a random sample of 2 rows using sample() with random_state=42 so results are reproducible.

Q8. Create a DataFrame from a list of dictionaries

Write code to create a DataFrame from the following list of student records and print it:

python
records = [
    {'Name': 'Ravi',  'Subject': 'Maths',   'Marks': 85, 'Semester': 1},
    {'Name': 'Priya', 'Subject': 'Maths',   'Marks': 92, 'Semester': 1},
    {'Name': 'Ravi',  'Subject': 'Physics', 'Marks': 76, 'Semester': 1},
    {'Name': 'Priya', 'Subject': 'Physics', 'Marks': 88, 'Semester': 1},
    {'Name': 'Arjun', 'Subject': 'Maths',   'Marks': 78, 'Semester': 2},
    {'Name': 'Meena', 'Subject': 'Physics', 'Marks': 90, 'Semester': 2},
]


After creating it:

a) Print the number of rows and columns.

b) Print all unique student names using a single method.

c) Print all unique subjects.

Expected output:

    Name  Subject  Marks  Semester
0   Ravi    Maths     85         1
1  Priya    Maths     92         1
2   Ravi  Physics     76         1
3  Priya  Physics     88         1
4  Arjun    Maths     78         2
5  Meena  Physics     90         2

(6, 4)

['Ravi' 'Priya' 'Arjun' 'Meena']

['Maths' 'Physics']

Q10. Combining Series operations with DataFrame

Write code to do all of the following in sequence:

a) Create the student DataFrame from Q5 (Name, RollNo, Maths, Physics, City).

b) Add a Total column (Maths + Physics).

c) Create a standalone Series called rank with values [3, 1, 5, 1, 4] indexed by the student names (Ravi, Priya, Arjun, Meena, Kiran). Note Priya and Meena are both rank 1.

d) Add this rank Series as a new column ClassRank to the DataFrame. Use the Name column or set Name as index first to align correctly.

e) Print the final DataFrame sorted by Total in descending order.

Expected output:

    Name  RollNo  Maths  Physics  Total  ClassRank
3  Meena     104     95       90    185          1
1  Priya     102     92       88    180          1
4  Kiran     105     88       79    167          4
0   Ravi     101     85       76    161          3
2  Arjun     103     78       82    160          5

 Q11. Read a CSV and inspect it

Name,RollNo,Maths,Physics,City

Kiran,105,88,79,Pune


Write code to:

a) Read the file into a DataFrame called df.

b) Print the shape.

c) Print the column names.

d) Print the data types of each column.

e) Print the first 3 rows.

Expected output:

(5, 5)

Index(['Name', 'RollNo', 'Maths', 'Physics', 'City'], dtype='object')

Name       object
RollNo      int64
Maths       int64
Physics     int64
City       object

2  Arjun     103     78       82  Bangalore

c) Print the total number of missing values across the entire DataFrame.

Name       0
RollNo     0
Maths      1
Physics    1

Write code to:

a) Read the Excel file from Semester1 sheet.

b) Print the DataFrame.

c) Add a Total column (sum of all three subjects).

d) Save the result as semester1_results.csv without index.

e) Print a confirmation message: "File saved as semester1_results.csv".

Expected output:

    Name  Maths  Physics  Chemistry

Q19. Write multiple DataFrames to separate Excel sheets

You have marks for two semesters:

Semester 1 — Ravi:85, Priya:92, Arjun:78, Meena:95, Kiran:88 (Maths)
Semester 2 — Ravi:90, Priya:88, Arjun:84, Meena:97, Kiran:91 (Maths)

Write code to:

a) Create two DataFrames sem1 and sem2, each with columns Name and Maths.

b) Write both to a single Excel file called all_semesters.xlsx with sheet names Semester1 and Semester2 using ExcelWriter.

c) Read both sheets back in and print them to verify.

Expected output after reading back:

--- Semester 1 ---
    Name  Maths
0   Ravi     85
1  Priya     92
2  Arjun     78
3  Meena     95
4  Kiran     88

--- Semester 2 ---
    Name  Maths
0   Ravi     90
1  Priya     88
2  Arjun     84
3  Meena     97
4  Kiran     91

Q20. End-to-end pipeline — read, process, save

Write a complete program that does the following in sequence:

a) Read students.csv (Name, RollNo, Maths, Physics, City).

b) Add a Total column (Maths + Physics).

c) Add an Average column (Total / 2, rounded to 1 decimal place).

d) Add a Result column: if Average >= 80 then Pass, else Fail.

e) Save the full processed DataFrame to processed_results.csv without index.

f) From the saved file, read back only the students who Passed and print them.

g) Print how many students Passed and how many Failed.

Expected output:

# Passing students read back from file:
    Name  RollNo  Maths  Physics  Total  Average Result
0   Ravi     101     85       76    161     80.5   Pass
1  Priya     102     92       88    180     90.0   Pass
3  Meena     104     95       90    185     92.5   Pass
4  Kiran     105     88       79    167     83.5   Pass

Pass     4
Fail     1
Name: Result, dtype: int64
